correctness.rationale: The geometric ten-curve configuration is known and reconstructed by blowing up four points; it gives a reduced connected nodal genus-six curve with 10 rational geometric components, 15 nodes, 30 branches, and divisor class -2K. The normalization point formula is valid over all finite extensions. The Pic0 connected torus has integral character lattice H1 of the Petersen graph. An exact six-cycle integer lattice basis and the signed edge chain action give integer matrices; seven explicit integral Frobenius bases have determinants ±1, proving the named torus isomorphisms and exact rational group products. The standalone standard-library proof checker exhausts all 120 S5 permutations, independently compares characteristic polynomials, checks 7 unimodular certificates, and reproduces all point-count tables; it printed VERIFY_OK. Computation is exhaustive in finite S5, not an extrapolation from small finite fields.

originality.rationale: Classical quintic del Pezzo Petersen configuration and Wiman–Edge reducible stable curve (2010/2012/2018) are explicitly attributed; their S5 action and rational representation are already known. Inspected sources and actual published-finding corpus searches do not state the exact seven integral Frobenius-lattice / finite-field torus isomorphism classes or associated cyclic rational-group decompositions and full boundary-zeta table. Rational representation and group order alone cannot certify a torus isomorphism. Explicit unimodular integral bases establish a distinct strict refinement. Unindexed implicit prior calculations remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: Rational S5 representation and curve geometry are strongly covered in prior literature; any claim of novelty of the Petersen graph, the genus-six boundary, or its rational character would be invalid.
An unindexed exact integral lattice/table or an implicit corollary of a specialist analysis of finite-field Wiman degenerations could anticipate some or all named torus products.
Accessible full-text checks focused on the highly relevant sections; no claim of an exhaustive search of every past article is made.
Only a self-review was performed, not an independent audit.

value.rationale: The complete isomorphism and rational abelian group classification for the natural connected generalized Jacobian of a canonical stable genus-six boundary is useful for arithmetic degeneration and Jacobian reduction. It resolves all seven finite-field forms and their boundary zeta functions; meaningful contrasts include type (3,2) a cyclic Fq6* Jacobian, type (5) a rationally point-free boundary with nontrivial split torus, and type (4,1) a single rational nonsplit node despite no rational component. Integral isomorphism, not merely rational character or point count, supplies the core value. No general downstream theorem is asserted.
